slides.heading: Stable Internships
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Famous Algorithms
slides.narration: Let's solve Stable Internships, a medium famous algorithms problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: N interns and n teams each rank the other side; produce a stable matching (Gale-Shapley with interns proposing).
slides.narration: Here's the problem. N interns and n teams each rank the other side; produce a stable matching (Gale-Shapley with interns proposing). Returns pairs intern, team .

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Gale–Shapley: interns propose in preference order; teams keep their favourite so far.
slides.narration: Gale–Shapley: interns propose in preference order; teams keep their favourite so far.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Brute force: check all n! matchings for stability
Precompute team rankings for O(1) comparisons
slides.narration: Checking all n factorial matchings is hopeless. Gale-Shapley has interns propose in preference order, and each team keeps the best proposal so far. Each intern proposes at most n times, so it's quadratic.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. Each proposes to the next team on their list
3. The team keeps the better intern
slides.narration: Step by step. First, queue of free interns. Second, each proposes to the next team on their list. Third, the team keeps the better intern. Fourth, rejected interns re-queue.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We build a rank table for teams, then a queue of free interns. Each free intern proposes to their next team. A free team accepts; otherwise the team keeps whichever intern it ranks higher and the other goes back in the queue. Finally we output intern-team pairs.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n squared. Space is O of n squared.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Always terminates with a perfect matching
slides.narration: Precompute each team's ranking of interns so comparisons are constant time. The result is the best stable matching for the proposing side.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
bullets: Explain why it's stable (no blocking pair)
Follow-up: who benefits — the proposing side
slides.narration: Be ready to argue stability: no intern and team both prefer each other over their matches. The proposing side gets its best stable outcome.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Gale–Shapley: interns propose in preference order; teams keep their favourite so far.
slides.narration: To recap Stable Internships: Gale–Shapley: interns propose in preference order; teams keep their favourite so far. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
